topic: How does the 45° scan range affect link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams?
consensus_response: The 45° scan range introduces significant challenges for link budget calculations, especially for edge-of-coverage users. The quasi-TE1 mode, with its increased scan angle and associated beam squint, results in higher side lobe levels (SLLs) and reduced gain compared to the quasi-TEM mode. At 45°, the SLLs can reach −8 dB, affecting the overall link budget by increasing interference and reducing the effective signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for edge users. To mitigate these effects, system designers can employ dynamic resource allocation strategies, optimize beamforming and error correction techniques, and balance the trade-offs between increased transmit power, error correction, and dynamic beamforming. By employing these strategies, system designers can effectively mitigate the effects of the quasi-TE1 mode and optimize the overall performance and capacity for edge-of-coverage users.
reference_context: The debate focused on the effects of a 45° scan range on link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams. The performance of two beamformers, one with a quasi-TEM mode and the other with a quasi-TE1 mode, was examined under various scanning conditions. The quasi-TE1 mode exhibited higher SLLs and beam squint, resulting in increased interference and reduced SNR for edge-of-coverage users.
